chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
“The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform wudu (ablution) with one mudd and perform ghusl with one saʿ, and the mudd is one and a half ratls, and the saʿ is six ratls.”
That is, the ratls of al-Madinah; thus it comes to nine Iraqi ratls, according to what he mentioned in the book.

key_terms.أَرْطَالَ الْمَدِينَةِ: the ratl measure according to the standard of al-Madinah
key_terms.رِطْلٌ: a unit of weight or measure used to quantify the mudd and saʿ
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a standard measure used here for the amount of water for ghusl
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a standard measure used here for the amount of water for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: How much water did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم use for wudu (ablution) and ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the amount of water the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used for wudu (ablution) and ghusl, giving the measures in mudd and saʿ. It also clarifies the equivalence of these measures in the ratl standard of al-Madinah and compares it to the Iraqi measure, making it relevant for rulings of ritual purity.
